navigable.name: Navigable River
navigable.description: A river reach that boats can use. Goods, news and orders travel quickly along it.

improvable.name: Shallows
improvable.description: Shoals and mill weirs: boats pass, but slowly.

barrier.name: Falls
barrier.description: Falls and great rapids that boats cannot pass.

starting_evidence.note: Maintained grain-navigation channels of the Grand Canal: shallows in this envelope start with a canal.
Basin channels kept open; the cataracts stay Falls.
Water-board authority documented from 1289. No industrial canals or steam drainage.

notes: Channel tiles take the topography of their World Builder state: navigable -> Navigable River, improvable -> Shallows, barrier -> Falls (impassable through the impassable_mountains list).

The channels are plain sea tiles: no water roads and no building act on them. The River Navigation Canal and the hidden navigation road types were removed 2026-10-13 (the AI did not use them and the player could not see what to improve; neither can build a road onto a sea tile, EU5 1.4).
Shallows with a bank in a starting_evidence envelope (the Grand Canal) start as Navigable River.

Proximity (2026-10-13, EU5 1.4 step costs, verified in game): a channel step is a sea step (30), divided by 1 + the proximity efficiency of the tile left. Navigable River +1.5 (30 -> 12, a vanilla river leg on land), Shallows +0.5 (20), Difficult Waterway modifier -0.75 on top of Navigable River (17); leaving the river 35 / 2.5 = 14. River ports get local_port_cost_distance_impact -0.5 on top of the harbour (boarding 35 -> ~17).

difficult_waterway.name: Difficult Waterway
difficult_waterway.description: A great tropical or strongly seasonal river. Floods, low water and sandbars slow the boats that carry news and orders.

river_port.name: River Port
river_port.description: A landing on a navigable river: boats from here join the waterway quickly.
